title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman of Emeco; distinguished only for clearance, which is given by the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Executive and non-executive directors other than the Chairman; distinguished for clearance (Chairman) and for the immediate ASX notification duty on any change in their interest in Securities.

tiers.name: All other Employees
tiers.description: All other officers, employees, consultants, advisors and contractors of Emeco and its subsidiaries; distinguished for clearance, which is given by the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Each close family member of an Employee and any company or trust which the Employee or close family member may control or influence; bound by the same restrictions and prohibitions as the Employee.

definitions.hedging_definition: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco

windows.start_anchor: 7 days prior to the end of the financial year
windows.end_anchor: one business day after the public release of Emeco's audited financial statements for that full year

windows.start_anchor: 7 days prior to the end of the half financial year
windows.end_anchor: one business day after the public release of Emeco's half year financial statements

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company Secretary may designate other black-out periods from time to time, and Emeco may impose a trading black-out at any time for any or all Employees, in its absolute discretion and without prior notice; the Company Secretary notifies Employees by email when a black-out period commences and expires, so imposition is not confidential once notified.

rules.detail: An OTC put/call is a transaction intended to hedge exposure and is banned outright, 'notwithstanding any provision of this Policy', for Securities issued to the Employee as part of remuneration (regardless of vesting). No clearance can override this.
rules.evidence: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco

rules.detail: The express hedge ban in 7.2(c) is confined by its wording to Securities issued as remuneration. For Securities acquired other than as remuneration (e.g. on-market purchases), an OTC derivative is not separately named but would need clearance under the general clearance regime for 'any proposed dealings in Securities'.
rules.evidence: Employees must obtain clearance for any proposed dealings in Securities by notifying the Company Secretary and seeking clearance

rules.detail: Absolute ban on hedging Securities issued as remuneration, with no vesting-based distinction and no clearance override.
rules.evidence: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco

rules.detail: Hedging Securities not issued as remuneration is not expressly named and falls back to the general clearance regime.
rules.evidence: Employees must obtain clearance for any proposed dealings in Securities by notifying the Company Secretary and seeking clearance

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation of remuneration-issued Securities is a transaction intended to hedge exposure and is banned outright.
rules.evidence: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco

rules.detail: Monetisation of Securities not issued as remuneration is not expressly named and falls back to the general clearance regime.
rules.evidence: Employees must obtain clearance for any proposed dealings in Securities by notifying the Company Secretary and seeking clearance

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-selling, applying 'notwithstanding any provision of this Policy'; no clearance route.
rules.evidence: engage in short-term trading and short-selling of Securities

rules.detail: Employees must not knowingly allow their Securities to be used by others for short-term trading and short-selling, which captures lending shares out for that purpose.
rules.evidence: knowingly allow their Securities to be used for short-term trading and short-selling

rules.detail: A CFD is not named but is caught either as a hedge of remuneration-issued Securities (absolute ban) or, if used speculatively, as short-term trading (absolute ban).
rules.evidence: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco

rules.detail: Absolute ban on funding the purchase of Securities with a margin loan; no clearance route. This is narrower than a general secured-financing ban -- it targets acquisition funding only.
rules.evidence: fund the purchase of Securities with margin loans

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Securities that could result in disposal without the Employee's consent is not banned outright; it is permitted provided clearance is obtained beforehand from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary (other Employees).
rules.evidence: enter into any arrangement where a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent, without receiving clearance from the Chairman (in respect of Directors) or the Company Secretary (in respect of all other Employees)

rules.detail: The clearance-based encumbrance clause is not limited to margin loans; it extends to any arrangement granting a security interest capable of forcing disposal without consent, so a bank loan secured on the collared shares is caught but clearable.
rules.evidence: enter into any arrangement where a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent, without receiving clearance from the Chairman (in respect of Directors) or the Company Secretary (in respect of all other Employees)

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term trading; no specific holding period is stated and no clearance route applies.
rules.evidence: engage in short-term trading and short-selling of Securities

clearance.approver: Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee
clearance.evidence: in respect of the Chairman – the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee ... Clearance will generally be effective for five business days or such other period as the approver considers appropriate

in respect of Directors – the Chairman ... Directors must ensure that any changes in a director's direct or indirect interest in Securities are immediately reported to the Company Secretary so that notification can be given to the ASX.
in respect of all other Employees – the Company Secretary.

short_term.evidence: engage in short-term trading and short-selling of Securities

exceptions.evidence: if the Employee can satisfy the Chairman that there are exceptional circumstances, such as financial hardship
transfers of Securities by a managed securities portfolio, where the Employee is not in a position to influence choices in the portfolio
transfers of Securities between an Employee and a Connected Person, or by an Employee to their superannuation fund
dealings under a dividend reinvestment plan where the Employee has given ongoing instructions to reinvest dividends
an acquisition of Securities under an employee incentive scheme
a disposal of Securities under an employee incentive scheme to a nominee of Emeco in accordance with the rules of the relevant employee incentive scheme
a disposal of Securities arising from an equal access buy-back
an acquisition of Securities under a pro rata issue
The restrictions in this Policy do not prevent Employees from accepting takeover bids or from selling Securities under a scheme of arrangement in respect of Emeco.

exemption_authority: The Chairman may excuse trading during a black-out period in exceptional circumstances such as financial hardship (clause 5.4(a)). Separately, granting a security interest over Securities (clause 7.2(b)) is permitted with prior clearance from the Chairman (Directors) or Company Secretary (other Employees), notwithstanding the general restrictions. Margin loans to fund acquisitions (7.2(a)), hedging of remuneration-issued Securities (7.2(c)), and short-term trading/short-selling (7.2(d)-(e)) have no exemption or clearance route anywhere in the Policy -- they apply 'notwithstanding any provision of this Policy'.

bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into any arrangement where a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent, without receiving clearance from the Chairman (in respect of Directors) or the Company Secretary (in respect of all other Employees)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike many peer policies that ban all secured financing outright, this Policy expressly permits granting a security interest over Emeco shares -- the funded collar's loan leg -- provided prior written clearance is obtained, giving a workable approval pathway for the loan.

bespoke_clauses.topic: absolute hedge ban on remuneration securities
bespoke_clauses.clause: enter into any transaction intended to hedge Employee's exposure to Securities, which have been issued to the Employee as part of the Employee's remuneration by Emeco
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Hedging (and by extension a collar) is banned outright, with no clearance override, for any Securities issued as remuneration -- a collar can only be considered over Securities held outside of incentive-plan issuance, e.g. shares bought on-market.

bespoke_clauses.topic: acquisition financing vs. security over existing shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: fund the purchase of Securities with margin loans (7.2(a)) ... a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent ... without receiving clearance (7.2(b))
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Distinguishes acquisition financing (banned outright) from encumbering already-held shares (clearable) -- a funded collar over existing vested shares is not a 'margin loan to acquire securities' and so is not caught by the absolute ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a security interest is granted over their Securities that could result in the disposal of their Securities without their consent
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's standard enforcement or forced-sale right under the collar's loan squarely triggers the clearance requirement, so the loan documentation and clearance request should address that risk up front.

bespoke_clauses.clause: those restriction and prohibitions also apply to each close family member and any company or trust which the Employee or close family member may control or influence
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or loan through a spouse, family trust or controlled company does not avoid the hedge ban or the clearance requirement for encumbrance.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar is realistically achievable for an Emeco director or employee, but only over shares that were not issued to them as remuneration, since clause 7.2(c) imposes an absolute, unwaivable ban ('notwithstanding any provision of this Policy') on any transaction intended to hedge exposure to Securities issued as part of remuneration, regardless of vesting. For shares acquired other than as remuneration, the put/call legs would fall under the ordinary clearance regime (clause 6): written clearance from the Chairman (for Directors), the Chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee (for the Chairman), or the Company Secretary (for other Employees), generally effective for 5 business days, outside black-out periods, and confirming no inside information is held. The loan leg is comparatively workable: clause 7.2(b) expressly contemplates granting a security interest over Securities that could force a disposal without consent, and permits it with the same Chairman/Company Secretary clearance -- more permissive than the outright secured-financing bans in many peer policies -- though funding the initial share purchase with a margin loan remains separately and absolutely banned (7.2(a)). Connected Persons (family members, controlled trusts/companies) are bound by the same rules, so the structure cannot be routed around the restrictions via family arrangements. Overall verdict: prohibited for remuneration-derived shares regardless of vesting, but permitted with prior Chairman/Company Secretary clearance (for both the derivative legs and the secured loan) over shares acquired other than as remuneration.
